title: The hammer, rebuilt to your description
question: You were right and I had it wrong: the blow was still taking a disc of rock out of the wall on every swing, with cracks drawn around the hole. That whole disc is gone. A swing now does exactly two things — open joints, and release any block the cracks have completely surrounded — so the only rock that ever leaves the wall comes off along a line you watched appear. First image is it animated, second is the same run swing by swing. Is this the mechanic?
context_md: Swing-by-swing on a solid stone face, hammer radius 7 (cracked = cells carrying a fissure, reach = how far from the impact, freed = cells released as whole blocks): swing 1 cracks 37 cells and releases NOTHING. Swing 2 releases 137 cells as 2 blocks. Swing 3 spreads the cracks to 61 cells, reach 25, releases nothing. Swing 4 releases another 131. Swing 5 spreads to 80 cells, reach 29. Swing 6 releases another 134. So the rhythm is crack, crack, block out, crack, crack, block out. Blocks are ~130 cells each; the gnome is 9x16 = 144, so these are about his size. Two things I had to fix to get there, both found by printing the swing-by-swing table rather than by looking: stone's grain is 13 cells but a swing only opened joints fully within 7, so a block's outline was ALWAYS partly outside the cracked zone and could never close; and growth read off current damage saturates — the front reached ring 3 and sat there for ever, freeing nothing after swing 2. The front now advances a ring per swing. NOT yet done, and I have not pretended otherwise: hitting a released block to break it smaller.
